current_example.title: Example: Combining the Power Rule of Exponents With Other Rules

q-100753.name: Question 1
q-100753.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the numerator using the product rule for exponents:

$$
\frac{(-5)^{7}\cdot (-5)^{5}}{(-5)^{8}}=\frac{(-5)^{7+5}}{(-5)^{8}}=\frac{(-5)^{12}}{(-5)^{8}}
$$

Then, we use the quotient rule for exponents:

$$
\frac{(-5)^{12}}{(-5)^{8}}=(-5)^{12-8}=(-5)^{4}
$$

q-100753.html:
Question 1
?

(−5)7⋅(−5)5(−5)8=

a
1(−5)
b
(−5)3
c
−5
d
(−5)4
e
(−5)5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we rewrite the numerator using the product rule for exponents:

(−5)7⋅(−5)5(−5)8=(−5)7+5(−5)8=(−5)12(−5)8

Then, we use the quotient rule for exponents:

(−5)12(−5)8=(−5)12−8=(−5)4
q-100753.knowledge_point: Combining the Product and Quotient Rules of Exponents

q-100752.name: Question 2
q-100752.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the numerator using the product rule for exponents:

$$
\frac{{9}^{4}\cdot {9}^{5}}{{9}^{6}}=\frac{{9}^{4+5}}{{9}^{6}}=\frac{{9}^{9}}{{9}^{6}}
$$

Then, we use the quotient rule for exponents:

$$
\frac{{9}^{9}}{{9}^{6}}={9}^{9-6}={9}^{3}
$$

q-100965.name: Question 3
q-100965.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the second factor using the power of product rule:

$$
{7}^{6}\cdot {(2\cdot 7)}^{3}={7}^{6}\cdot {2}^{3}\cdot {7}^{3}
$$

Finally, we apply the product rule for exponents, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{6}\cdot {2}^{3}\cdot {7}^{3} & ={7}^{6}\cdot {7}^{3}\cdot {2}^{3} \\  & ={7}^{6+3}\cdot {2}^{3} \\  & ={7}^{9}\cdot {2}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-100965.html:
Question 3
?

76⋅(2⋅7)3=

a
718⋅23
b
76⋅2
c
79⋅23
d
73⋅23
e
79⋅2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we rewrite the second factor using the power of product rule:

76⋅(2⋅7)3=76⋅23⋅73

Finally, we apply the product rule for exponents, and simplify:

76⋅23⋅73=76⋅73⋅23=76+3⋅23=79⋅23

q-100964.name: Question 4
q-100964.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the second factor using the power of product rule:

$$
{(7\cdot 9)}^{4}\cdot {7}^{6}={7}^{4}\cdot {9}^{4}\cdot {7}^{6}
$$

Finally, we apply the product rule for exponents, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{4}\cdot {9}^{4}\cdot {7}^{6} & ={9}^{4}\cdot {7}^{4}\cdot {7}^{6} \\  & ={9}^{4}\cdot {7}^{4+6} \\  & ={9}^{4}\cdot {7}^{10}\end{aligned}
$$

q-68959.name: Question 5
q-68959.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the numerator using the power of product rule:

$$
\frac{(5\cdot 2)^{4}}{{5}^{3}}=\frac{{5}^{4}\cdot {2}^{4}}{{5}^{3}}=
$$

Next, we rewrite the fractional part of our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{5}^{4}\cdot {2}^{4}}{{5}^{3}} & =\frac{{5}^{4}}{{5}^{3}}\cdot {2}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the first fraction using the quotient rule for exponents, and then we simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{5}^{4}}{{5}^{3}}\cdot {2}^{4} & ={5}^{4-3}\cdot {2}^{4} \\  & ={5}^{1}\cdot {2}^{4} \\  & =5\cdot {2}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$
